# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance when working with code in this repository.

Kinoshka — movie catalog SPA with a home feed, search, filters, and detail pages (overview, cast, media).

## Git workflow

`main` is protected — changes land only via pull request, never a direct push. Work on a branch and open a PR to merge into `main`.

## Commands

A `Makefile` at the project root wraps all pnpm scripts. Prefer `make` over direct `pnpm` calls.

```bash
make dev          # start dev server with HMR
make build        # type-check (tsc -b) then Vite production build
make typecheck    # type-check only (tsc -b)
make build-only   # Vite production build, no type-check
make lint         # oxlint over all TS/TSX files
make preview      # serve the production build locally
make install      # install dependencies
make hooks        # install husky git hooks (pnpm exec husky)
make clean        # remove dist and node_modules
make check        # lint + build (full validation)
make generate-api # regenerate API client from OpenAPI spec (re-run after spec changes)
make test         # run Vitest once
make test-watch   # run Vitest in watch mode
make coverage     # run Vitest with coverage report
make audit        # pnpm audit (prod deps, high severity)
make analyze      # ANALYZE=true production build → dist/stats.html (bundle treemap)
make size         # pnpm exec size-limit — enforce per-chunk size budgets against dist/
make knip         # pnpm exec knip — unused exports/deps/files detector
make e2e          # pnpm exec playwright test — run E2E specs (requires make build-only first, see e2e section)
make e2e-install  # pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
```

**Commit hooks:** husky + lint-staged run `oxlint --fix --deny-warnings` on staged `*.{ts,tsx}` files pre-commit. Commit messages are enforced by commitlint (`@commitlint/config-conventional`); use `pnpm commit` (commitizen, `cz-conventional-changelog`) for a guided conventional-commit prompt instead of `git commit` directly.

## Architecture

React 19 + TypeScript 7 + Vite 8 single-page app.

**React Compiler is enabled.** The compiler (`babel-plugin-react-compiler`) runs via `@rolldown/plugin-babel` alongside `@vitejs/plugin-react` (see `vite.config.ts`). It automatically memoizes components and hooks, so manual `useMemo` / `useCallback` / `memo` calls are unnecessary and should be avoided — the compiler handles that.

**TypeScript strictness:** `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, and `erasableSyntaxOnly` are all on. `erasableSyntaxOnly` means TypeScript-only syntax that can't be stripped without transformation (e.g. `enum`, `namespace`, parameter properties) is forbidden — use plain JS-compatible constructs instead.

**TypeScript style:** use `type` (not `interface`) for all type definitions.

**Icons** are sprite-based: `public/icons.svg` holds an SVG sprite; components reference symbols via `<use href="/icons.svg#<id>" />`. See the [Icons](#icons) section for available IDs.

**Fonts:** `index.html` loads three Google Fonts — Instrument Serif (`--font-serif`), Instrument Sans (`--font-display` / `--font-body`, the default UI font), JetBrains Mono (`--font-mono`). Use these; don't add new font imports.

**Path aliases** correspond to FSD layers and are configured in both `vite.config.ts` and `tsconfig.app.json`: `@app`, `@pages`, `@widgets`, `@features`, `@entities`, `@shared`. Use these aliases for all cross-layer imports.

## Project structure

The project follows [Feature-Sliced Design](https://feature-sliced.design/):

```
src/
├── app/          # providers, router, global styles
├── pages/        # route-level components
├── widgets/      # large reusable UI sections (header, mobile-chrome, movie-rail, search-sidebar)
├── features/     # user-facing interactive features (e.g. catalog-filter)
├── entities/     # business-domain objects (e.g. movie — types, data, UI)
└── shared/       # cross-cutting utilities and primitives (lib/, ui/)
```

Import direction: `pages → widgets → features → entities → shared`. Never import upward.

**Page-slice `model/` facade.** When a page needs to combine data/logic from more than one downward slice (e.g. both `@features/*` and `@entities/*`), put the composing hook in that page's own `model/` directory (`src/pages/<page>/model/`) rather than in `@entities` or `@features` — a lower slice can't legally import a higher one, but the page slice can import both downward. Example: `src/pages/search/model/useMovieCatalog.ts` composes `filtersToParams` (`@features/catalog-filter`) with `getSearchMovies`/`getMoviesPage` (`@entities/movie`) into the one hook the `/search` UI calls. Not exported through a public `index.ts` — page-internal only.

## Routing

React Router 7 (`react-router@^7.15.1`). Route config lives in `src/app/router.tsx`; provider setup in `src/app/providers.tsx`.

Routes: `/` (home feed), `/search` (search + filters), `/movie/:id` (detail — overview, cast, media tabs), `/favorites` (favorited movies), `/popular` (this week's popular movies, with rank badges), `/recommendations` (rule-based picks derived from favorites).

## API layer

The API client is auto-generated from the Kinopoisk OpenAPI spec using `@siberiacancode/apicraft`.

**Generated files** — never edit manually, regenerate instead:

- `src/shared/api/instance.gen.ts` — `ApiInstance` class built on `@siberiacancode/fetches`. `make generate-api` prepends `// @ts-nocheck` to this file after generation, so it isn't type-checked.
- `src/shared/api/types.gen.ts` — all request/response types

**Hand-written wrapper:** `src/shared/api/client.ts` instantiates `apiClient` from `instance.gen.ts` (base URL / API key from env) and installs a response interceptor that normalizes error messages. This file is safe to edit and is where cross-cutting API behavior (auth headers, error shaping) lives.

**Config:** `apicraft.config.ts` reads `APP_API_URL` from `.env.local` as the OpenAPI spec source.

**Environment:** create `.env.local` at the project root before running `make generate-api`:

```
APP_API_URL=<Kinopoisk OpenAPI spec URL>
VITE_API_KEY=<your API key>
VITE_BASE_URL=<base URL for API requests>
```

Import the client via `@shared/api`.

## Responsive pattern

Mobile-first CSS, not paired components: every page and widget is **one** component, one CSS module, and the mobile layout is the unconditional base — desktop overrides live in `@media (min-width: 720px)` blocks on top of it. There is no `*Desktop`/`*Mobile` pair to maintain in parallel; a single React tree covers both breakpoints, and visual/behavioral differences that CSS can express (layout, spacing, hover-only controls via `@media (hover: hover)`/`@media (hover: none)`) are expressed in CSS, not via a JS `isMobile` branch. Follow this pattern when adding new page or widget components — see `docs/plans/20260827-mobile-first-adaptive-layout.md` for the migration that replaced the old paired-component pattern.

- Mobile breakpoint: **720px** (`MOBILE_BREAKPOINT` in `src/shared/lib/viewport/useViewport.ts`) — reused as the `min-width: 720px` media query value everywhere the split is CSS-only, so the visual breakpoint didn't shift during the migration.
- `useViewport()` (`@shared/lib`) is **not** deleted, but its consumers are narrowed to exactly two point-in-time JS forks — cases where CSS genuinely cannot express the difference, because it's not a layout/visual variant but a decision about which component mounts (and its side effects):
  1. **`src/app/layouts/AppLayout.tsx`** — chooses whether to mount `Header` (`@widgets/header`) or `MobileHeader`+`BottomNav` (`@widgets/mobile-chrome`). This can't be CSS-only (`display: none` on the unused variant) because `Header` unconditionally runs a `?q`-debounce effect that writes/clears the URL search param regardless of `variant`/visibility — a hidden-but-mounted `Header` would keep silently mutating `?q` on routes where that's not wanted. `AppLayout` renders exactly one of the two chrome variants per route (via its `ROUTE_CHROME`/`MOVIE_CHROME`/`SEARCH_CHROME` config, keyed by path), so pages themselves no longer branch on viewport at all.
  2. **`src/pages/search/ui/Search/Search.tsx`** — chooses `SearchSidebar` (`@widgets/search-sidebar`, always-visible aside) vs. a mobile filter bar + `BottomSheet` (portal, its own open/close state, triggered by a button). These are genuinely different UX patterns, not a CSS variant of the same tree — same reasoning extends to the sort control (desktop `SortSelect` dropdown vs. a mobile `BottomSheet` list).
  - Any other former `useViewport()` call site (the six old `*Page.tsx` branches, `MovieRailDesktop`/`MovieRailMobile`'s `ArrowBtn` visibility, etc.) was resolved to pure CSS during the migration — e.g. `MovieRail`'s scroll arrows are hidden via `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` instead of an `isMobile` check, which is actually more accurate than a width-based fork (a wide touch tablet shouldn't see hover-only arrows either).

## Component structure

Every UI component lives in its own directory with a co-located CSS module:

```
ComponentName/
├── index.tsx              # named export of the component
└── ComponentName.module.css
```

Sub-components (e.g. `NavPill`, `ArrowBtn`) get their own nested directories following the same pattern.

Each slice in `widgets/` and `features/` exposes a **public API** via an `index.ts` at the slice root:

```
src/widgets/header/
├── index.ts               # export { Header } from './ui/Header'
└── ui/
    ├── Header/
    │   ├── index.tsx
    │   └── Header.module.css
    └── NavPill/
        ├── index.tsx
        └── NavPill.module.css
```

**Imports must always use the slice's public index, not internal paths:**

```ts
// ✓ correct
import { Header } from '@widgets/header'
import { useFilterState } from '@features/catalog-filter'

// ✗ wrong — reaches into internals
import { Header } from '@widgets/header/ui/Header'
```

**Stretched-link pattern (`Card`):** to avoid nesting interactive elements (`<button>` inside `<a>`, invalid HTML and bad for a11y/keyboard nav), the card's outer container is a plain `<div>` and the `react-router` `<Link>` wraps only the title text, giving it a real accessible name. The link gets a `::after` pseudo-element (`position: absolute; inset: 0`) that stretches its hit-area over the whole card via `position: relative` on the container; action buttons stay DOM siblings of the link (not descendants) with a higher `z-index` so they still receive clicks. Follow this pattern for any future card-like component that combines a primary navigation target with secondary action buttons.

**Dual-thumb range slider pattern (`YearRangeSlider`, `@features/catalog-filter/ui`):** for a two-handle range control, use two overlapping native `<input type="range">` elements instead of a hand-rolled pointer-drag implementation — it's less code and gets keyboard support (arrows, Home/End), focus, and screen-reader semantics for free. Cross-link `min`/`max` between the two inputs (the "from" input's `max` is the live value of "to", and vice versa) so the browser itself refuses to let the thumbs cross, with no manual clamping math. Give each `<input>` `pointer-events: none` except its own thumb pseudo-element (`::-webkit-slider-thumb`/`::-moz-range-thumb` get `pointer-events: auto`), so both thumbs stay independently draggable while fully overlapping; paint the native track transparent and render the visible track/fill as separate absolutely-positioned `div`s driven by inline `style` percentages. Commit to the parent's `onChange` on release (`onMouseUp`/`onTouchEnd`) **and** `onKeyUp` (keyboard changes fire neither mouseup nor touchend), gated on the committed pair actually differing from the last-committed one (Tab-focus alone delivers a `keyup` with no value change). Clamp/normalize incoming values into the slider's UI bounds on both initial state and the props-resync effect, since out-of-range or reversed (`from > to`) values would otherwise desync React's controlled `value` from the native DOM value.

**Theming pattern (`@features/theme`):** the app supports `light`/`dark`/`system`, resolved to `light`/`dark` and applied as a `data-theme` attribute on `<html>` (not `<body>`) via `useTheme()`'s effect. `src/app/styles/global.css` keeps the unconditional `:root { ... }` as the dark palette (no attribute = dark) and adds a parallel `:root[data-theme='light'] { ... }` block overriding the same variable names, each block also setting `color-scheme: dark`/`color-scheme: light` alongside the token overrides so native controls (scrollbars, both `<input type="range">` thumbs in `YearRangeSlider`) render in the matching OS-level skin instead of an OS-default one that clashes with the app theme. `index.html` runs a synchronous inline `<script>` in `<head>`, before `<div id="root">`, that reads `localStorage`, resolves the theme, and sets `data-theme` before first paint — this prevents a flash of the wrong theme (FOUC) that a post-mount `useEffect` alone couldn't avoid. Because of this, any new CSS must reference `var(--token)` and never hardcode a hex/rgba color — a hardcoded color silently ignores `data-theme='light'` and stays wrong in the light theme.

**`rankBadge` slot placement in `Card` (unified across breakpoints).** `Card` takes an optional `rankBadge?: ReactNode` prop (rendered by `PopularBadge` for `/popular`'s rail and page), grouped with `.ratingBadge` in a `.topBadges` flex row in the top-left corner — the same placement on both mobile and desktop, since `Card`/`MobileCard` were merged into one component (see [Responsive pattern](#responsive-pattern)) and the bottom corner stays reserved for the single favorite button (`.favoriteBtn`, top-right on mobile / bottom-right on desktop) and the hover-only `.actions` row (desktop only, `bottom: 10px`). `.topBadges` is deliberately kept at the implicit `z-index: auto` (not matching `.title::after`'s `z-index: 1`) so the stretched-link overlay still paints on top of it and the corner stays clickable; giving `.topBadges` an explicit `z-index: 1` would tie-break by DOM order in the card's `isolation: isolate` stacking context and create a dead click zone. Any future overlay badge added to `Card` should check which corner is actually free (and whether it needs to out-stack the stretched-link overlay) before picking a z-index.

**`IconButton` lives in `@shared/ui`, not `@widgets/header`.** It moved there from `src/widgets/header/ui/IconButton/` during the theme-toggle work because it was never Header-specific (its `.module.css` was already fully `var(--...)`-driven), and `@features/theme`'s `ThemeToggle` needs to render it — `features/*` can't import from `widgets/*` under this repo's `pages → widgets → features → entities → shared` import direction, so a shared, generic component like this has to live at the `shared/` layer to be usable from both `widgets/header`/`widgets/mobile-chrome` and `features/theme`.

## Styles

All styles use **CSS Modules** (`ComponentName.module.css`). Import as `import s from './ComponentName.module.css'` and apply via `className={s.className}`.

- Hover states → CSS `:hover` pseudo-class (not `useState` + inline style toggling)
- Conditional classes → template literals: `` `${s.btn} ${active ? s.active : ''}` ``
- Dynamic values (e.g. computed heights) → inline `style` only when truly necessary
- CSS variables (`var(--font-body)`, etc.) defined in `src/app/styles/global.css` — use them, don't hardcode

## Icons

`public/icons.svg` currently contains only social icons:

```
bluesky-icon  bluesky-clip  discord-icon  documentation-icon
github-icon   social-icon   x-icon
```

For UI icons (search, arrow, close, chevrons, play, star, etc.) use the React components from `@shared/ui` (e.g. `SearchIcon`, `CloseIcon`, `StarIcon`, `PlayIcon`, `ChevronLeftIcon`). Do not add them to the sprite.

## Error tracking (Sentry)

Roadmap `2.5.1`. Error tracking only — no performance tracing (`browserTracingIntegration`/`tracesSampleRate`) is wired up; that's `2.5.2`, deliberately out of scope here because the app has a parametrized route (`/movie/:id`) that would need `reactRouterBrowserTracingIntegration` to avoid one transaction per movie.

**`make typecheck` used to check 0 files — fixed while building this Sentry feature.** The root `tsconfig.json` is solution-style (`{ "files": [], "references": [...] }`); `make typecheck` ran `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` against it, and without `-b` that type-checks **0 files** (verified via `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --listFiles`), so CI's `typecheck` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) was a no-op the whole time and CI's `build` job never ran `tsc` at all — no CI job actually type-checked `vite.config.ts`, `sentry.config.ts`, or `src/**`, which is exactly the gap this Sentry work would have shipped into unchecked. Fixed narrowly: `make typecheck` now runs `pnpm exec tsc -b`, which builds both referenced projects (`tsconfig.app.json` → all of `src/`, `tsconfig.node.json` → `vite.config.ts`/`sentry.config.ts`) — the same command `pnpm build` already ran first, just now also wired into the dedicated CI `typecheck` job. No other CI/tsconfig architecture was touched.

- **`initSentry()`** (`src/app/sentry.ts`) is called once at module top level in `src/app/providers.tsx`, before `Providers` is defined — not as an import-time side effect inside `sentry.ts` itself, so it stays testable with different `import.meta.env` values. It reads `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` and returns immediately unless `import.meta.env.PROD && dsn` — a no-op in dev/test, and a no-op in any prod build where `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` isn't set (e.g. a fresh checkout without `.env.local`). This repo's own `.env.local` now carries a real DSN (see "CSP headers + security headers" below) — Sentry is live in prod builds made from it. When it does run, it calls `Sentry.init({ dsn, release: __APP_RELEASE__, environment: import.meta.env.MODE, sendDefaultPii: false, beforeSend: scrubApiKeyHeader })`.
- **`GlobalErrorBoundary`** (`src/app/GlobalErrorBoundary.tsx`) wraps `<RouterProvider>` in `providers.tsx` with `Sentry.ErrorBoundary`, using the existing `ErrorState` (`@shared/ui`) as its fallback for visual consistency with the point-in-time `AsyncBoundary` fallbacks used elsewhere. It's a separate top-level component rather than a change to `shared/ui/ErrorBoundary` — that primitive already backs every `AsyncBoundary` (rails, `/search`, `/movie/:id`), and touching it for Sentry would widen the blast radius of this feature well beyond what the roadmap item asks for.
- **Env variables:**
  - `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` — client-side, read in the browser bundle; safe to expose (Sentry DSNs are meant to be public).
  - `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` / `SENTRY_ORG` / `SENTRY_PROJECT` — build-time only, read via `loadEnv` in `vite.config.ts`; never inlined into the client bundle. `sentryVitePlugin` is only added to the Vite `plugins` array when `command === 'build'` and all three are set — so `vite dev` and Vitest never load it, and a build without these three set (e.g. a checkout with no `.env.local`, or one missing them) simply skips source-map upload rather than failing. This repo's own `.env.local` now sets all three to real values, so `make build` here does upload source maps.
- **Release tagging:** the release string is built exactly once, in `vite.config.ts`, as `` `kinoshka@${version}+${gitSha}` `` — `version` read directly from `package.json` via `fs.readFileSync` (not `process.env.npm_package_version`, which isn't reliably set across `make build`/`make build-only`/CI), `gitSha` from `execSync('git rev-parse --short HEAD')` with a `try/catch` fallback to `'unknown'` so a build without `.git` available doesn't fail. The same string is passed both to the browser SDK (via a `define: { __APP_RELEASE__: JSON.stringify(release) }` constant, declared ambient in `src/vite-env.d.ts` and read by `initSentry()`) and to `sentryVitePlugin({ release: { name: release } })`, so the SDK and the source-map upload always tag the same release — otherwise the plugin would default to the bare git SHA and uploaded source maps wouldn't match the release recorded on incoming events. The pure parts of this logic — `buildRelease()`, `isSentryEnabled()` (the `command === 'build' && <all three creds>` gate), and `resolveBuildSourcemap()` — live in `sentry.config.ts` (root-level, next to `vite.config.ts`, not under `src/`, following the same `<tool>.config.ts` naming as `apicraft.config.ts`/`vite.config.ts`) specifically so they have real unit test coverage (`sentry.config.test.ts`); `vite.config.ts`'s `defineConfig` callback itself stays a thin composition of these plus the effectful bits (`execSync`, `readFileSync`) that aren't worth mocking.
- **Source maps:** `build.sourcemap` is `'hidden'` when the Sentry plugin is active, `false` otherwise — never unconditionally `true`. `'hidden'` writes `.map` files without adding a `//# sourceMappingURL=` comment to the built chunks, and `sentryVitePlugin`'s `filesToDeleteAfterUpload: ['./dist/**/*.map']` removes the `.map` files from `dist/` after upload — so source maps never ship to end users but errors in production still deminify in the Sentry dashboard.
- **PII scrubbing:** `scrubApiKeyHeader()` (`src/app/sentry.ts`), wired as `beforeSend`, strips `X-API-KEY`/`x-api-key` from `event.request.headers` if present. This is defense-in-depth, not a fix for an existing leak — with `sendDefaultPii: false` (the SDK default, set explicitly) the browser SDK doesn't attach request headers to events on its own; the scrub only guards against some future integration or manually-attached context doing so. Separately, and _not_ addressed by this: `VITE_API_KEY` (`@shared/api/client.ts`) is inlined into the client bundle by Vite and will therefore also be present in any source maps uploaded to Sentry — an accepted limitation until the BFF phase (Phase 5), not a regression introduced by Sentry integration.

## Web Vitals + Analytics (Plausible)

Roadmap `2.5.2`. Deliberately not Sentry Performance — see the `2.5.1` note above about `/movie/:id` needing `reactRouterBrowserTracingIntegration`; `web-vitals` (a thin wrapper over `PerformanceObserver`) sidesteps that entirely since it has no notion of routes. Analytics is Plausible, not PostHog — privacy-first, no cookie banner, minimal setup (one script tag + `window.plausible()`).

`src/shared/lib/analytics/` — three files, re-exported through `src/shared/lib/index.ts` (the public `@shared/lib` barrel):

- **`analytics.ts`** — `initAnalytics()`, `trackEvent(name, props?)`, `trackPageview()` are public (re-exported from `@shared/lib`). `isAnalyticsEnabled()` (`import.meta.env.PROD && Boolean(VITE_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN)`, same shape as `initSentry`'s gate) is an internal module detail — it's re-exported from `src/shared/lib/analytics/index.ts` only so `reportWebVitals.ts` can import it from within the same module, but it is **not** re-exported from the public `src/shared/lib/index.ts` barrel; it has no consumer outside `analytics/`.
- **`reportWebVitals.ts`** — `reportWebVitals()`, also public.

**Queue-stub ordering.** `initAnalytics()` sets Plausible's official queue-stub on `window.plausible` **synchronously**, before inserting the `<script>` tag — a dynamically-inserted `<script>` executes asynchronously regardless of `defer`, so without the stub `window.plausible` stays `undefined` for several milliseconds after `initAnalytics()` returns. Without it, the very first `trackPageview()` (fired from `AppLayout`'s mount effect) and early web-vitals (LCP fires early) would be silently dropped on almost every session — not an edge case, the common case. The stub pushes call arguments onto `window.plausible.q`, which the real script drains once it loads. `initAnalytics()` also guards against a duplicate `<script>` insertion via `document.getElementById('plausible-analytics-script')` (HMR-safe, same pattern as `reportWebVitals`'s module-level `reported` flag below).

**`.manual.js` script + manual pageview.** The script loaded is `plausible.io/js/script.manual.js`, which disables Plausible's automatic pageview/outbound-link tracking — `trackPageview()` (`trackEvent('pageview')`, `'pageview'` being Plausible's reserved event name) is instead called explicitly on every route change from `AppLayout` (see integration points below). Without this, only the very first page load of a session would register as a pageview in an SPA.

**`reportWebVitals`'s dynamic import.** `src/shared/lib/analytics/index.ts` (and hence `reportWebVitals`) is re-exported through the public `@shared/lib` barrel that's imported from nearly every module in the app, so `reportWebVitals.ts` imports `web-vitals` via `await import('web-vitals')` rather than a static top-level import — a static import would pull the whole package into the main chunk just for one prod-only call site. A module-level `reported` flag guards against re-registering the `onLCP`/`onINP`/`onCLS` callbacks on a repeat call (e.g. HMR), mirroring `initAnalytics()`'s `getElementById` guard. **Failure handling:** the dynamic `import()` is chained with a `.catch()` that resets `reported` back to `false` and logs via `console.error` — a network failure loading the `web-vitals` chunk (offline, ad-blocker, CDN outage) would otherwise leave an unhandled promise rejection and permanently disable web-vitals reporting for the rest of the session (since `reported` would stay `true` forever); the rollback lets a later call to `reportWebVitals()` retry instead.

**Event naming.** All four events use lowercase names (`'pageview'`, `'search submitted'`, `'filter changed'`, `'favorite added'`, `'web vital: lcp'`/`'web vital: inp'`/`'web vital: cls'`) — Plausible goals are literal strings, expensive to rename after data accumulates, so the case is fixed once here rather than left inconsistent across call sites. `reportMetric` (private to `reportWebVitals.ts`) multiplies CLS by `1000` before rounding — the raw CLS value is a unitless fraction like `0.05`; `*1000` gives an integer, convenient as a Plausible custom-event prop. LCP/INP are sent as-is (rounded, no scaling).

**Accepted limitation: no `sendBeacon` delivery for late vitals.** Neither `web-vitals` nor this integration uses `navigator.sendBeacon`. `onCLS`/`onINP` (and often `onLCP`) frequently fire on `visibilitychange`/page-hide, when a normal XHR/fetch request from the Plausible script can be cancelled by the browser as the tab closes. This is a known delivery gap for late-firing vitals, not a bug — fixing it would mean patching Plausible's own script internals, out of scope here.

- **Env variables:**
  - `VITE_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN` — client-side, read in the browser bundle; safe to expose, same reasoning as `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` above.

**`interface Window` — deliberate exception to `type`-not-`interface`.** `src/vite-env.d.ts` declares `window.plausible`'s shape via `interface Window { plausible?: ... }` rather than `type`, with a Russian WHY-comment above it: global declaration merging against a built-in ambient type (`Window`) only works through `interface` — `type` cannot extend it. This is the one deliberate carve-out from the repo-wide "`type`, not `interface`" rule (see [TypeScript style](#architecture)).

**Four event integration points** (none of them live in `@entities`/`@features` importing upward — `useFilterState`/`useFavorites` legally import `@shared/lib` downward, `AppLayout`/`Search.tsx` are `app`/`pages`-layer, also legal to import downward):

- **page view** — `src/app/layouts/AppLayout.tsx`, the single layout component every route passes through. A `useEffect` keyed on `location.pathname` only (not `location.key`/`search`) calls `trackPageview()` — keying on the full location would spam a pageview on every `?q` debounce write from `Header` or every filter click on `/search`, since those mutate the URL without changing the page.
- **search submitted** — `src/pages/search/model/useSearchAnalytics.ts`, a page-slice hook (not exported from a public `index.ts`, page-internal only per the "Page-slice `model/` facade" convention) called from `Search.tsx` right after `query` is derived from `searchParams.get('q')`. There's no single "submit" action to hook — `HeroSection` fires on explicit Enter/click, `Header` writes `?q` live on a 250ms debounce with no discrete submit event — so `useSearchAnalytics` observes the committed `query` instead. It first runs `query` through its own `useDebouncedValue(query, 800)` (800ms, well past `Header`'s 250ms) before comparing against the last-tracked value via a `useRef` (the same transition-ref pattern as `usePageSync.ts`) — without that extra debounce, typing one word would commit several intermediate non-empty `?q` values in quick succession, each of which a bare transition-ref comparison would count as a separate "submitted" event. The event carries no `props` (query text isn't sent) to keep tracked data minimal, in line with Plausible's privacy-first positioning. The ref resets to `''` whenever the settled query is empty, so re-entering the same text after clearing the field tracks again.
- **filter changed** — `applyFilters` in `src/features/catalog-filter/model/useFilterState.ts`, the single point where `FilterState` is committed to the URL (`setFilters`/`toggleGenre`/year-range reset/rating reset all funnel through it). `setSort` is a separate function and is **not** tracked — the roadmap's four-event list names only "filter changed", sort isn't in scope. `trackEvent` fires unconditionally on every `applyFilters` call, including true no-op commits (e.g. `resetFilters()` on already-empty filters, or `setFilters()` called with a value identical to current state) — accepted, since the roadmap's instruction is "single commit point, track there", not "track only on an actual diff".
- **favorite added** — the add branch of `toggle(id)` in `src/features/favorites/model/useFavorites.ts` (the branch where `id` was not already in the favorited set). `add(id)` itself is not instrumented — it currently has no `.tsx` caller (the real "add to favorites" affordance goes through `toggle`), so tracking a dead code path was skipped rather than invented ahead of a real consumer.

## Performance budgets + bundle visualization

Roadmap `2.5.3`. See `docs/plans/20260912-performance-budgets-bundle-visualization.md` for the full discovery/rationale; this section captures the decisions that stick. The plan deliberately reordered the roadmap's checklist: route-based code splitting first (creates chunks to measure), then visualization (see what landed), only then budgets (measured, not guessed) — before this work the entire app (6 pages, `react-router`, `@sentry/react`, `zod`, etc.) built into one 555 kB chunk, with Rolldown itself warning about it.

- **`lazyNamed`** (`src/shared/lib/lazyNamed/lazyNamed.ts`, re-exported from `@shared/lib`) — a thin adapter over `React.lazy()`: `lazyNamed(factory, exportName)` is `lazy(() => factory().then(m => ({ default: m[exportName] })))`. `React.lazy()` requires a module with a `default` export, but every page slice (`@pages/*`) exports its component by name (`export { HomePage } from './HomePage'`, not `default`) — a bare `lazy(() => import('../pages/home'))` doesn't resolve. `src/app/router.tsx` uses it for all 6 routes, e.g. `lazyNamed(() => import('../pages/home'), 'HomePage')`. `<P extends object>` (no `any`, per `.oxlintrc.json`'s `"no-explicit-any": "error"`) keeps the generic sound without a literal `any`.
- **`<Suspense>` boundary in `AppLayout.tsx`** wraps `<Outlet/>` (the single point every route passes through) with `fallback={<Spinner/>}` — this is a **code**-loading Suspense (waiting for a page's JS chunk), not a data one; each page still has its own `<AsyncBoundary>` around its async data section (see "Loading / Empty / Error everywhere" elsewhere in this doc), and the two don't replace each other.
  - **Accepted risk:** react-router navigations run inside `startTransition`. On a **page-to-page** navigation (not the first load), React defers committing the whole tree — including `AppLayout` itself — until the new chunk resolves, so the `<Spinner/>` fallback, the `activeNav`/`BottomNav` highlight, and the `trackPageview()` effect (`AppLayout.tsx`) all lag behind the click instead of updating immediately. On slow networks this reads as a briefly unresponsive UI with no loading indicator. This is accepted as-is — page chunks are KB-sized, not seconds of load time — but is documented here rather than left as a silent side effect.
- **`build.rolldownOptions.output.codeSplitting.groups`** (`vite.config.ts`) — a `{ name: 'vendor', test: /node_modules/ }` group, a `{ name: 'shared', test: /\/(widgets|features|entities|shared)\// }` group, and one explicit group per page (`page-home`, `page-movie`, `page-favorites`, `page-popular`, `page-recommendations`, `page-search`, each `test` matching that page's directory under `src/pages/`). Two deliberate non-choices, plus one correction from code review:
  - **Not `advancedChunks`** — the installed `rolldown@1.0.2` marks `advancedChunks` `@deprecated` in favor of `codeSplitting`, and warns that if both are set, `advancedChunks` is ignored.
  - **Not a separate `chunkFileNames`** — it's a global pattern applied to _every_ chunk, not just the ones being renamed; since chunks without an explicit group get a name derived from their content (and all 6 page slices are imported through an identically-named `index.tsx` barrel, risking collisions like `page-index-*.js`/`page-index2-*.js`), the fix is giving each page group (and `vendor`/`shared`) its own explicit `name` in `codeSplitting.groups` instead — `[name]-[hash].js` then just works, and neither name is touched by a global rename rule.
  - **`shared` group added after code review found the first version defeated the whole feature.** The initial `codeSplitting.groups` had only `vendor` + the 6 page groups — no group for cross-page code (`AppLayout`'s `Header`/`MobileHeader`/`BottomNav`, `@entities/movie`'s `Card`/`Poster`, favorites/theme/genre-dictionary storage, etc.). None of that code matched `/node_modules/` or a single page's directory, so Rolldown's common-chunk heuristic arbitrarily assigned it to whichever page group came first in the list (`page-home`) — and because `AppLayout` (part of the eager entry, not behind any `lazy()`) statically imports pieces of it, that "page" chunk ended up statically imported by the entry itself and by every other page chunk. Concretely: `dist/assets/index-*.js` and all five non-home page chunks contained a static `import{...}from"./page-home-*.js"`, so visiting `/favorites` still eagerly downloaded page-home's ~18.7 kB gzip on every load — the opposite of per-route isolation. Adding an explicit `shared` group ahead of the page groups (matching `@widgets`/`@features`/`@entities`/`@shared`) gives that code one real, always-loaded-once chunk instead: verified post-fix that `index-*.js` and every page chunk now import only `rolldown-runtime`/`vendor`/`shared`, never another page chunk.
  - **`web-vitals` group added ahead of `vendor` after a later code review found the catch-all `vendor` group had silently re-eagered it.** `test: /node_modules/` on `vendor` matches every package unconditionally, including `web-vitals` — even though `reportWebVitals.ts` (`src/shared/lib/analytics/`, see "Web Vitals + Analytics" above) deliberately loads it via `await import('web-vitals')`, specifically so it stays out of the always-downloaded chunk. Before this fix, `vendor-*.js` measurably contained web-vitals internals (confirmed by grepping the built chunk for `onHidden`/`PerformanceObserver`) and no dedicated `web-vitals-*.js` chunk existed at all — `dist/index.html` `modulepreload`s `vendor`, so the dynamic `import()` bought nothing; the library downloaded eagerly on every page load regardless. Fix: an explicit `{ name: 'web-vitals', test: /node_modules\/web-vitals\// }` group ordered before `vendor` (same "explicit named group beats the catch-all" pattern as the page groups vs. `vendor` itself). Post-fix, `web-vitals-*.js` is a real dedicated chunk (~3.4 kB gzip), referenced only via a dynamic `import()` call inside `shared-*.js` (never a static `import` statement) and absent from `index.html`'s `modulepreload` list — confirmed via build output and grep. `vendor` shrank accordingly (~140.4 kB → ~137.4 kB gzip).
- **`ANALYZE` env flag** — `make analyze` runs `ANALYZE=true pnpm exec vite build`. `isAnalyzeEnabled({ command, env })` (`bundle.config.ts`, a root-level module next to `sentry.config.ts` kept separate so bundle-specific and Sentry-specific pure logic don't mix in one file) is `command === 'build' && env.ANALYZE === 'true'` — same shape as `isSentryEnabled`, with its own `bundle.config.test.ts`, following the `sentry.config.ts` precedent of pulling pure predicates out of `vite.config.ts` specifically so they're unit-testable (see "Error tracking (Sentry)" above). When enabled, `vite.config.ts` adds `rollup-plugin-visualizer`'s `visualizer({ filename: 'dist/stats.html', gzipSize: true, brotliSize: true, template: 'treemap' })` to `plugins` — a Rollup plugin, not a Rolldown-native one, but it ran clean against the Rolldown build with no compatibility issues found. It's gated behind the flag rather than always-on so ordinary builds/CI don't pay for generating a report nobody's looking at.
- **`size-limit` budgets** (`package.json`, `"size-limit"` section, `@size-limit/file`) — 10 entries: `entry` (`dist/assets/index-*.js`), `vendor` (`dist/assets/vendor-*.js`), `web-vitals` (`dist/assets/web-vitals-*.js`), `shared` (`dist/assets/shared-*.js`), and one per page chunk (`page-home`, `page-movie`, `page-favorites`, `page-popular`, `page-recommendations`, `page-search`), each `gzip: true` with `path`, not `import` (`@size-limit/file` has no `import` mode — it only measures the already-built `dist/`, it doesn't bundle anything itself). Every limit is that entry's real measured gzip size from a post-code-split build, plus 15% (the middle of the roadmap's suggested 10-20% buffer) — not a number picked in advance. **Why `@size-limit/file` instead of the roadmap's literal `@size-limit/preset-app`:** `preset-app` pulls in `@size-limit/time`, which spins up headless Chrome/`estimo` to measure execution time — unneeded weight and CI flakiness risk when the budget here is only about bytes, not runtime. **Re-measured after the `shared`-group fix above** — adding `shared` shrank every page chunk that used to carry absorbed cross-page code (e.g. `page-home` dropped from ~18.7 kB to ~2.6 kB gzip once `Header`/`Card`/etc. moved out into `shared`; `page-search` dropped from ~8.5 kB to ~6.1 kB), so all 8 old limits were re-derived from the new measured sizes and a 9th `shared` entry (~19.6 kB measured, 22.6 KB limit) was added. **Re-measured again after the `web-vitals`-group fix above** — `vendor` shrank from ~140.4 kB to ~137.4 kB gzip once `web-vitals` moved out into its own chunk (limit lowered 162 KB → 158 KB), and a 10th `web-vitals` entry (~3.4 kB measured, 3.95 KB limit) was added — this one _is_ budgeted, unlike `rolldown-runtime` below, because it's a real vendor library that can grow with a `web-vitals` version bump, not fixed bundler plumbing. None of the old numbers describe the current build.
- **`rolldown-runtime-*.js`** (a small Rolldown-emitted module-runtime helper chunk, ~0.6 kB gzip, present in every build) is **deliberately not covered by any `size-limit` entry** — same treatment as per-page CSS chunks (see Task 3 note below): it isn't application code, it's fixed bundler-runtime plumbing that doesn't grow with app features, so budgeting it would just be noise. If a future Rolldown version changes what this chunk contains, revisit.
- **Per-page CSS chunks are also not budgeted.** `codeSplitting.groups` only groups JS; CSS still splits into an entry `index-*.css` plus one file per page/shared group (e.g. `page-movie-*.css`, `shared-*.css`) as a side effect, but `size-limit` in this plan only measures JS (`path` globs all end in `.js`). Accepted gap, not tracked here — CSS budget is a candidate for a future plan if it starts mattering.
- **`knip.jsonc`** (note: `.jsonc`, not `knip.json` — chosen specifically because `knip.json` can't carry the comments below linking `ignore` entries back to the AGENTS.md sections that justify them). `entry` is `src/main.tsx` **plus** `**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` **plus** the root config files (`vite.config.ts`, `sentry.config.ts`, `apicraft.config.ts`, `bundle.config.ts`) — without the test files and root configs, knip flags most test-only devDependencies (`vitest`, `msw`, testing-library, `oxlint`, `husky`, `commitlint`, `apicraft`) as unused, since nothing in the app's own entry graph reaches them. `ignore` covers exports this repo intentionally keeps without a current consumer rather than deleting: `src/shared/api/*.gen.ts` (generated files this doc already says never to hand-edit — "unused" isn't a reason to touch them either), the whole `@shared/config` module (`useFeatureFlag()`/`FeatureGate`/`FeatureName` — see "Feature flag not wired" above, same precedent as `popularThisWeek`/`toggleTheme`), and the public barrels of `catalog-filter`/`favorites`/`theme`/`shared/ui` (re-exports like `getFilterFromSearchParams`/`UseFavoritesResult`/`useTheme`/`ErrorBoundary` that are documented public API in "Key public APIs" below even where no external call site currently exists). Everything knip flagged that _wasn't_ one of these documented-intentional cases was fixed at the source instead of ignored: `src/App.tsx`/`src/App.css`/`src/assets/{hero.png,react.svg,vite.svg}` (an untouched Vite scaffold nothing imported) were deleted, and a handful of exports with exactly one same-file consumer (`fetchCatalogCursor`, `GENRE_LABELS`, `FILTER_AND_SORT_URL_KEYS`, `CatalogMode`, `SessionCacheEntry`, plus dead barrel re-exports of `YEAR_SLIDER_MAX`/`YEAR_SLIDER_MIN` and `SessionCache`) had their unnecessary `export` keyword removed.

## CSP headers + security headers

Roadmap `2.5.4`. See `docs/plans/20260912-csp-security-headers.md` for the full discovery/rationale (including the two factual corrections made during planning — the `img-src` hosts and the real, non-placeholder Sentry DSN); this section captures the decisions that stick. The project is a pure Vite SPA with no server of its own (SSR is a future Phase 4), deployed on **Vercel** — headers go through `vercel.json`'s `headers` field, not an HTML `<meta>` tag, since `report-uri` isn't supported in meta-CSP in any browser.

- **`vercel.json` (root) is the single source of truth.** It now carries a `headers` entry for `source: "/(.*)"` with four headers: `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. `vercel.json` is static JSON — Vercel doesn't substitute env vars into it at deploy time — so every host in the policy is a hardcoded literal, verified against the real running app rather than guessed from docs/spec.
- **`img-src` hosts were verified by live requests, not by reading the committed OpenAPI spec.** The spec suggests `https://st.kp.yandex.net` as "the poster domain", but a live `GET /v1.5/movie` against `https://api.poiskkino.dev` (using the real key from `.env.local`) showed posters/backdrops (and `getMovieImages()`/`/v1.5/image`, rendered by `MediaTab`) actually come from `https://avatars.mds.yandex.net`; `st.kp.yandex.net` is the **person-photo** domain (`persons[].photo` → `CastMember.photo` → `CastTab.tsx`'s `<img src={c.photo}>`, confirmed via a live `GET /v1.5/movie/666`). Both hosts are in `img-src`. `https://image.tmdb.org` (the DTO's `logo.url`/`logo.previewUrl`) is **deliberately not added** — `mapDtoToMovieDetail.ts` never maps `logo` into `MovieDetail` and no component renders it, so adding a host for an unused field would only widen the attack surface with no functional need.
- **`script-src` uses a SHA-256 hash, plus `'unsafe-inline'` for legacy-browser fallback.** The only inline script in the app is the anti-FOUC theme script in `index.html`'s `<head>` (see the Theming pattern note above) — it's allowed via a hash source (`'sha256-...'`) computed with `node:crypto` over the exact text content between the `<script>` tags, the same algorithm browsers use for CSP hash-source matching. `vercel-headers.test.ts` (root) does **not** hardcode this hash a second time — it re-reads `index.html`, recomputes the hash itself, and compares it against whatever hash source is present in `vercel.json`'s `script-src`, so a future edit to the inline script that forgets to update `vercel.json` fails the test instead of silently going stale. **Invariant, verified by build:** `vite build` does not transform/minify this classic inline `<script>` tag, so the hash computed from source `index.html` is identical to the one in `dist/index.html` — if a future HTML-minifier plugin is added, recompute and re-verify this invariant, since minification would change the tag's exact byte content and invalidate the hash. **`'unsafe-inline'` was added to `script-src` after running the policy through [CSP Evaluator](https://csp-evaluator.withgoogle.com/)** (its own suggested follow-up, see below) — per CSP2+, a browser that understands the `'sha256-...'` hash source ignores `'unsafe-inline'` entirely when it's present alongside a hash/nonce, so this is a no-op backward-compat addition for pre-CSP2 browsers, not a weakening of the policy for any browser that actually enforces it.
- **`style-src` includes `'unsafe-inline'`, deliberately weaker than `script-src`.** `YearRangeSlider` and other runtime-computed inline `style` attributes (see the Styles section above) have non-static values — nothing to hash — and CSP's `style-src` governs both `<style>` tags and the `style` HTML attribute, so the only practical option is `'unsafe-inline'`. This is accepted as strictly less dangerous than an equivalent `script-src` hole — it only enables CSS injection, not arbitrary script execution.
- **`connect-src` also includes `https://fonts.googleapis.com`/`https://fonts.gstatic.com`, not just the stylesheet/font hosts they serve.** `index.html` does `<link rel="preconnect">` to both — Chromium checks resource hints (`preconnect`/`dns-prefetch`) against `connect-src`, not just `style-src`/`font-src`, so omitting them from `connect-src` would fire a CSP violation report on every single page load (the exact opposite of the "clean soak period before enforce cutover" goal of this task). This was caught by code review after the initial version only added the two hosts to `style-src`/`font-src`.
- **`assetsInlineLimit` → `img-src` dependency.** Vite's default `assetsInlineLimit` (4096 bytes) can inline small assets into CSS as `data:` URIs, which would require `data:` in `img-src`. Verified against the current build (`dist/assets/*.css`) that no such `url(data:...)` exists today, so `img-src` doesn't need `data:` — but this is a non-obvious dependency on build config, not a permanent guarantee; revisit if a future asset crosses the inline threshold.
- **`report-uri` is a Sentry security-report endpoint**, built from the **public** part of the real `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` in `.env.local` (org `o4512052151844864`, project `4512052165607429`, US ingest region) in Sentry's documented format `https://<ingest-host>/api/<project_id>/security/?sentry_key=<public_key>`. Committing the public key is safe by the same principle already stated for `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` above ("Sentry DSNs are meant to be public"). No `report-to`/`Reporting-Endpoints` — `report-uri` alone gives the needed browser coverage with the least complexity, and it's what Sentry itself recommends for CSP reports.
- **SRI (Subresource Integrity) — deliberately not applied to any current external resource.** The Google Fonts stylesheet serves UA-negotiated content (different `woff2` per browser), so pinning a hash would break loading for some UAs; `plausible.io/js/script.manual.js` is an unversioned URL that Plausible can update server-side at any time, so pinning a hash would break loading on their next release. Revisit if a future pinned/versioned CDN script is added.
- **Testing pattern:** unlike `sentry.config.ts`/`bundle.config.ts` (pure functions extracted from `vite.config.ts` because `vite.config.ts` is their real build-time consumer), `vercel.json` has no such consumer — it's a static file Vercel reads at deploy time, not a build artifact — so there's no parallel `csp.config.ts` module duplicating the same string. Instead, `vercel-headers.test.ts` (root) reads `vercel.json` itself as the only source of truth and asserts directly against its parsed content (directives/hosts, the recomputed script hash, the other three headers), including an edge-case test that a broken/incomplete parsed config throws a clear error rather than an opaque `undefined`.
- **Header is `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`, not enforcing, on purpose.** The roadmap calls for a 1-2 week soak period on production, monitored via the Sentry endpoint above, before cutting over to the enforcing `Content-Security-Policy` header — that cutover is out of scope for this work and tracked as an open item in `plans/roadmap.md` 2.5.4.
- **External-fact coupling, not caught by any test:** if `VITE_BASE_URL` (the API domain) or the Sentry org/project/region ever change, `connect-src` and `report-uri` in `vercel.json` must be updated by hand — this is an external fact, not a repo-internal desync a test could catch.
- **Post-completion follow-up: ran the policy through [CSP Evaluator](https://csp-evaluator.withgoogle.com/), per the plan's Post-Completion checklist.** Three findings, addressed as follows:
  - `'unsafe-inline'` added to `script-src` (see the hash bullet above) — a no-op backward-compat addition for pre-CSP2 browsers, ignored by any browser that actually enforces the hash.
  - `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` added to the policy — hardens against DOM-XSS injection sinks (`innerHTML`, etc.) by requiring a Trusted Types policy for any script-executing sink. Low risk here since the app has no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in `src/` (verified during code review); being `Report-Only`, this can't break anything even if some current or future dependency turns out to rely on a raw sink — it'll only generate violation reports to investigate.
  - **`strict-dynamic` — deliberately not adopted, accepted limitation.** CSP Evaluator flags `https://plausible.io` in `script-src` as a bypassable host allowlist and suggests `'strict-dynamic'` with nonces/hashes instead. `strict-dynamic` needs a **per-request nonce** to work (a static hash alone doesn't give the propagating trust `strict-dynamic` relies on for dynamically-inserted scripts like Plausible's), and `vercel.json`'s `headers` are static JSON evaluated once at deploy time — Vercel does not run request-time logic to mint a fresh nonce per response. Achieving this would require moving CSP header generation into a Vercel Edge Middleware (or a real backend), which is out of scope for this pure-SPA, static-`vercel.json` setup. Revisit if/when the project gains a server-side request path (Phase 4 SSR, mentioned above, or an Edge Middleware adopted for another reason).

## E2E тесты (Playwright + axe-core)

Roadmap `2.5.5`. See `docs/plans/20260912-e2e-playwright-axe.md` (moved to `docs/plans/completed/` once this task closes) for the full discovery/rationale; this section captures the decisions that stick.

- **Real API, not an in-browser MSW mock.** Playwright hits the same live `https://api.poiskkino.dev` the production app hits, under a preview build served from `dist/` — no `msw/browser` + service-worker infrastructure to maintain, and the smoke tests exercise real response shapes end to end. **Quota risk:** the demo tier is 200 requests/day (see "Data state" above), and a full local run across every spec/project costs roughly 40-50 requests. This is mitigated three ways: the CI job triggers only on `pull_request` (not also on `push: main`, which would just re-run an already-passed check and double the daily spend on every merge), a `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: true` scoped per shard cancels stale reruns on repeated pushes to the same PR, and the smoke suite stays deliberately small (one flow per journey, one `checkA11y` per spec rather than per tab/interaction). If quota still doesn't hold up in practice, `page.routeFromHAR` (HAR-replay) is the documented fallback — considered and rejected at planning time because it would quietly change the "real API" decision, not because it's technically unworkable (see Post-Completion in the plan).
- **CI job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `e2e`) is gated `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`.** There's no job-level `on:` key in GitHub Actions — trigger scoping has to go through `if:`. Two deliberate restrictions bundled into that one condition: it never runs on `push: main` (same quota reasoning as above — that push already passed as a PR), and it never runs on a fork PR, because fork PRs don't get repo secrets — the build would still succeed but `VITE_API_KEY` would be empty and every spec would fail on 401/403 against the real API. This is an accepted limitation (forks aren't supported), not a "not wired up yet" gap.
- **`vite preview`, not `vite dev`.** `playwright.config.ts`'s `webServer` runs `pnpm exec vite preview --port 4173 --strictPort` over an already-built `dist/` — the same code-splitting/minification path that actually ships, and the same "test against preview/deploy, not dev server" posture `2.5.6`'s Lighthouse job will reuse. The `webServer` command deliberately does **not** build — the build is a separate explicit `make build-only` step before every `playwright test` invocation (both locally and in CI), so a stale `dist/` never masks a real regression (e.g. the a11y fixes below not actually being in the served bundle). CSP headers are **not** exercised by this suite — `vercel.json`'s `headers` are applied by the Vercel hosting layer, not by `vite preview`.
- **A11y baseline fixed before the first spec landed (Task 2).** A pre-implementation axe pass (cross-referenced against source reading, to avoid a redundant API-quota-burning pre/post run — see the plan's Task 2) found seven `button-name` (axe `critical` impact) violations, all icon-only buttons with no accessible name, fixed as follows:
  - `Header.tsx` — the search icon `IconButton` (`SearchIcon`, opens `/search`) got `aria-label='Open search'`.
  - `Header.tsx` — the notifications-bell `IconButton` (`BellIcon`, currently no `onClick`) got `aria-label='Notifications'`.
  - `Card.tsx` — the Eye/preview `CardBtn` (`square` variant, `EyeIcon`) got `ariaLabel='Preview'`. `CardBtn`'s accessible name comes only from its `ariaLabel` prop or a visible `label` (rendered as a `<span>`, which the Rate/Add buttons already had) — Eye had neither.
  - `MobileHeader.tsx` — the `.backBtn` (`<ChevronLeftIcon>`, calls `onBack`) got `aria-label='Back'`.
  - `Pagination.tsx` — the prev/next chevron buttons got `aria-label='Previous page'`/`aria-label='Next page'`.
  - `ActiveFilterChips.tsx` — the chip-remove buttons (both the `chipRemove` and `chipCompactRemove` variants) got a dynamic ``aria-label={`Remove ${c.label}`}``.
  - `BottomSheet.tsx` — the `.closeBtn` (`CloseIcon` in `.titleRow`) got `aria-label='Dismiss'`, deliberately **not** `'Close'` — the adjacent backdrop button already has `aria-label='Close'`, and reusing the same name inside one open sheet would make `getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' })` resolve to two elements (same class of problem as the favorite-button `aria-label` collision across cards, see below).
  - Each fix got a matching unit-test assertion (`getByRole('button', { name: ... })`) in the component's existing `.test.tsx` file, except `BottomSheet` (no `.test.tsx` exists for it).
- **Desktop/mobile split via `testDir`, not a duplicated suite.** `playwright.config.ts` defines two projects: `chromium` (`testDir: './e2e'`, `testIgnore: '**/mobile/**'`) and `Mobile Safari` (`devices['iPhone 13']`, its own `testDir: './e2e/mobile'`) — the mobile project physically can't see specs outside `e2e/mobile/`. Roadmap only asks for mobile coverage on `/`, `/search`, `/movie/:id`, so `e2e/mobile/smoke.spec.ts` is a small, separate, trimmed-down suite rather than the whole desktop suite re-run under a phone viewport (which would just double API spend with no added coverage).
- **`vite.config.ts`'s Vitest `test.exclude` uses `configDefaults`.** `test.exclude: [...configDefaults.exclude, 'e2e/**']` (imported from `'vitest/config'`) rather than a hand-copied default-exclude list, so Vitest's own defaults don't drift out of sync on a future Vitest upgrade. Without this, Vitest's default `**/*.{test,spec}.*` glob would pick up `e2e/*.spec.ts` and fail with "Playwright Test did not expect test() to be called here" — verified in Task 1 by temporarily removing the exclude and confirming the failure, then confirming the same 82-file/687-test count with and without it once restored.
- **CI needs two secrets/vars:** `VITE_API_KEY` (GitHub Secret, not yet added to the repo — see Post-Completion) and `VITE_BASE_URL` (passed as a plain literal, `https://api.poiskkino.dev`, directly in the job's `env:` — not a secret, same precedent already used for `SENTRY_URL` in the `build` job). Neither `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` nor `VITE_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN` is passed to the e2e build step — both `initSentry()`/`initAnalytics()` no-op on an empty value, so the preview build stays silent and doesn't send CI-run noise into the production Sentry/Plausible projects.
- **`--shard=N/4`, not the roadmap's literal `--workers=4`.** The roadmap asks for parallel workers; in a CI setup with independent jobs (rather than one long-lived machine), Playwright's `--shard` flag is the direct analog — parallelism across machines instead of threads within one. `ci.yml`'s `e2e` job runs a `matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]`, each shard independently checking out, installing, and building (no `dist/` artifact sharing between shards — simpler than artifact plumbing, and the SPA build takes seconds). The `concurrency` group is keyed on `matrix.shard` as well as `github.ref` — without the shard in the key, all four shards of one run would land in the same concurrency group and `cancel-in-progress` would make them cancel each other instead of just canceling a stale rerun of the same shard.
- **Coverage extended beyond the roadmap's literal 6 journeys to all 6 SPA routes.** The roadmap names home/search/filter/detail/favorites-persist/theme-toggle, but the app has 6 routes total (`/`, `/search`, `/movie/:id`, `/favorites`, `/popular`, `/recommendations`) — `/popular` and `/recommendations` weren't covered by any of the 6 named journeys, and the original favorites journey only toggled the heart button on `/`, never opening `/favorites` itself. Three additions close that gap: `e2e/popular.spec.ts` (Task 7 — checks the first card's rank badge, `PopularBadge`'s `role='img'` `aria-label` like `'Position 1'`), `e2e/recommendations.spec.ts` (Task 8 — a fresh/empty browser context hits the `EmptyState` branch before any API call, since `Recommendations.tsx` short-circuits on `ids.length === 0` ahead of `useFavoriteMovies()`), and `e2e/favorites.spec.ts` gained an explicit `page.goto('/favorites')` + card-presence check after the reload step, on top of the heart-toggle check on `/`.
- **Stable selectors, no `data-testid`.** Nothing in the app renders one, and none was added — every spec selects via `role`/`label`/`placeholder`/text, or via the one exception documented in the plan's Technical Details: `page.locator('a[href^="/movie/"]').first()` for "the first movie card," since a bare `getByRole('link').first()` resolves to the header logo or a rail title link before it ever reaches a card. Where multiple cards share the same `aria-label` (e.g. every un-favorited card's favorite button says `"Add to favorites"`), specs scope to one card via `.filter({ has: ... })` chains rather than climbing CSS classes — see the plan for the full locator.
- **`e2e/utils/a11y.ts`'s `checkA11y(page)`** runs `AxeBuilder` and asserts zero violations with `impact === 'critical'` — not zero violations of any severity, since the roadmap's acceptance bar is "no critical violations," and third-party resources (Google Fonts) can produce minor/moderate noise that shouldn't fail the suite.
- **Known local limitation, not a CI gap:** on this project's development machine (macOS 14.4, `mac14-arm64`), Playwright refuses to install/run a non-frozen WebKit build, so the `Mobile Safari` project can't be run end-to-end locally — validated instead by running the same three mobile specs against Chromium with an emulated mobile viewport. CI runs on `ubuntu-latest`, where WebKit installs and runs normally; this is scoped to the local machine, not a defect in the mobile project's config.
- **`make e2e-install` always runs unconditionally in CI**, even on a Playwright-browser-binary cache hit — the `actions/cache` step (keyed on the installed `@playwright/test` version) only covers the downloaded browser binaries, not the system libraries `--with-deps` installs (apt packages WebKit needs, etc.); `playwright install` itself already skips re-downloading cached binaries, so running it unconditionally still gets the caching benefit without risking a broken WebKit on a cache hit.
- **`e2e`/`knip.jsonc`/`tsconfig.node.json` wiring:** `playwright.config.ts` and `e2e/**/*.ts` are in `tsconfig.node.json`'s `include` (no DOM lib added — specs use only Playwright's `Page`/`Locator` API, never raw DOM types like `document`/`HTMLElement`), and `playwright.config.ts` + `e2e/**/*.spec.ts` are in `knip.jsonc`'s `entry` (with `e2e/**/*.ts` also in `project`, so knip can resolve imports into helper modules like `e2e/utils/a11y.ts`) — otherwise knip flags `@playwright/test`/`@axe-core/playwright` as unused devDependencies, the same pattern already established for other test-only tooling (see "Performance budgets" above).
- **Not yet a required branch-protection check.** The `e2e` job exists and is wired into CI, but promoting it to a required status check for `main` is deliberately deferred to Post-Completion, pending the `VITE_API_KEY` secret being added to the repo and a few PRs' worth of observed quota/stability.
